subject: general
question: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)** is a regional intergovernmental organization and geopolitical union of states in **South Asia**. It was established with the signing of the **SAARC Charter** in **Dhaka** on **8 December 1985**.
 
• The organization currently has **8 member countries**: **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• **Afghanistan** became the **8th member** of **SAARC** during the **14th SAARC Summit** held in **New Delhi** in **April 2007**. Prior to this, there were only seven founding members. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• **Bhutan** is one of the founding members of the association and has been an active participant since its inception in **1985**. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **China** holds the status of an **Observer Country** in **SAARC**, but it is not a formal member of the association. The association currently has **9 observers**, including **Australia**, **China**, the **European Union**, **Iran**, **Japan**, **Mauritius**, **Myanmar**, **South Korea**, and the **United States**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Nepal** is a founding member and currently hosts the **SAARC Secretariat**, which was established in **Kathmandu** on **16 January 1987**. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of SAARC:**
 
 
• The primary objective of **SAARC** is to promote the **welfare of the peoples of South Asia** and to improve their quality of life through **accelerated economic growth**, **social progress**, and **cultural development** in the region.
 
• It aims to provide all individuals the opportunity to live in dignity and to realize their full potentials by strengthening **collective self-reliance** among the countries of **South Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Secretariat and Administration:**
 
 
• The **SAARC Secretariat** is headed by a **Secretary-General**, who is appointed by the **Council of Ministers** from Member States in alphabetical order for a **three-year term**.
 
• The first **Secretary-General** was **Abul Ahsan** from **Bangladesh**. The current **Secretariat** is located in **Kathmandu**, **Nepal**.
 
 
 
• **Specialized Bodies of SAARC:**
 
 
• **South Asian University (SAU)**: An international university established by the eight member nations of **SAARC**, located in **India** (**New Delhi**).
 
• **SAARC Development Fund (SDF)**: Its primary objective is to promote the welfare of the people of the **SAARC region**, with its secretariat located in **Thimphu**, **Bhutan**.
 
• **SAARC Arbitration Council (SARCO)**: An inter-governmental body located in **Islamabad**, **Pakistan**, to provide a legal framework for the settlement of commercial and trade disputes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Principles of SAARC:**
 
 
• Cooperation within the framework of the association is based on respect for the principles of **sovereign equality**, **territorial integrity**, **political independence**, and **non-interference** in the internal affairs of other states.
 
• Decisions at all levels in **SAARC** are taken on the basis of **unanimity**, and **bilateral and contentious issues** are excluded from the deliberations of the association.
 
 
 
• **SAARC Charter Day:**
 
 
• Every **year**, **8 December** is observed as **SAARC Charter Day** to mark the adoption of the **SAARC Charter** in **1985**.
 
 
 
• **South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA):**
 
 
• **SAFTA** was reached at the **12th SAARC Summit** at **Islamabad**, **Pakistan** on **6 January 2004**. It aims to reduce **customs duties** of all traded goods to **zero percent** by the **year 2016**.
